title: Armed Squatter Removal Team Faces Felony Charges In California Raid

 By iHeartRadio
 November 20, 2026
 Photo: Pla2na / iStock / Getty Images A squatter removal operation in San Bruno, California, has led to felony charges against the owner and an employee of ASAP Squatter Removal after a dramatic nighttime raid on a home. James Jacobs , 40, owner of ASAP Squatter Removal, and Arthur Gutierrez Jr ., 40, are accused of breaking into a home on Allen Drive in January with a team equipped with pistols, samurai swords, and tactical gear.
 Prosecutors allege that Jacobs’ team used a battering ram to force entry into the property around 2 a.m., confronting Silvino Manzano Jr . and his friends, who were living there. The group, dressed in black and partially masked, told the occupants they had 15 minutes to leave, claiming they were the new tenants . The confrontation included threats with firearms and swords. Manzano Jr. called 911 during the raid, and the police responded, detaining members of the removal team but initially treating the matter as a civil dispute.
 Further investigation revealed body camera videos uploaded by Jacobs that showed his team preparing for a "breach and clear" operation and entering the house with weapons drawn. Police later determined that at least two members of the team had threatened residents with guns. San Mateo County District Attorney Stephen Wagstaffe is prosecuting the case, emphasizing the dangers involved when weapons are brought into such situations.
 Jacobs and Gutierrez now face charges including burglary, assault with a semiautomatic handgun , false imprisonment, and weapons violations. A judge dismissed kidnapping charges but ordered both men to stand trial on seven felony counts each. Jacobs has pleaded not guilty and is out on $50,000 bail. Gutierrez’s case was diverted to a veterans court due to mental health considerations.
 The incident has highlighted growing tensions across California over squatting and property rights, as well as the risks of bypassing legal eviction processes. District Attorney Wagstaffe stated that even when eviction is difficult, “as an organized society, we cannot let [vigilante actions] occur.” The trial is set to continue, with Jacobs maintaining his innocence and arguing that he is a victim of political prosecution.
